claimText: The instruction to 'continue' IS NOT an invitation to land and the pilot must wait for landing clearance or initiate a missed approach.
normalizedRuleClaim: CONTINUE is not a landing clearance; the pilot must either receive landing clearance or initiate a missed approach.
notes: Strong vertical-slice candidate: behavior is already represented by distinct instructions and post-clearance/pre-clearance regulation split tests.

claimText: If the runway is obstructed at the time of the 'final' report (at 4 NM or less) but is expected to be available in good time, the controller will delay landing clearance.
normalizedRuleClaim: If the runway is obstructed at the final report but expected to be available in good time, the controller delays landing clearance.
notes: Good test oracle: obstruction present before landing clearance should produce continue-approach companion handling, not landing clearance.

claimText: In such circumstances, the pilot is to be informed of the aircraft or vehicles on the runway.
normalizedRuleClaim: When runway occupation drives go-around circumstances, the pilot is informed of aircraft or vehicles on the runway.
notes: Existing tests assert obstruction-driven go-around behavior; vertical slice can check whether emitted reason/trace evidence is sufficiently source-unit-grounded.

claimText: In the event of missed approach being initiated by the pilot, the phrase ‘going around’ shall be used.
normalizedRuleClaim: When the pilot initiates a missed approach, the phrase 'going around' is used.
notes: Good source-unit anchor for the named radio witness already used by G3 tests.

claimText: An aircraft operating VFR is to continue into the normal traffic circuit unless instructions are issued to the contrary.
normalizedRuleClaim: A VFR aircraft continues into the normal traffic circuit unless instructed otherwise.
notes: Existing tests check recovery Downwind and commitment regression; vertical slice can make the source-unit evidence explicit.

claimText: Unless instructions are issued to the contrary, an aircraft operating VFR will continue in the normal traffic circuit.
normalizedRuleClaim: Unless instructed otherwise, a VFR aircraft going around continues in the normal traffic circuit.
notes: Duplicates the CAP413 VFR recovery idea from ICAO9432; useful for citation redundancy and source-priority comparison.

claimText: Unless instructions are issued to the contrary, an aircraft on an instrument approach will carry out the missed approach procedure.
normalizedRuleClaim: Unless instructed otherwise, an aircraft on an instrument approach carries out the missed approach procedure.
notes: Accepted and testable in principle, but current golden surface is VFR-heavy; this should probably wait for IFR/missed-approach procedure modeling.

claimText: When in the circuit, the pilot shall transmit: (position in circuit, e.g. DOWNWIND/FINAL);
normalizedRuleClaim: When in the circuit, the pilot transmits the circuit position, such as DOWNWIND or FINAL.
notes: Good bridge from source unit to protocol event and golden trace.

claimText: A 'FINAL' report shall be made when an aircraft turns onto final within 7 km (4 NM) from touchdown, or at 7 km (4 NM) if no landing clearance was received at the 'LONG FINAL' point.
normalizedRuleClaim: A FINAL report is made when turning final within 7 km/4 NM, or at that distance if no clearance was received at LONG FINAL.
simulatorConcept: Final report timing and landing-clearance readiness
notes: Current tests observe FINAL/landing behavior but do not appear to assert the 4 NM timing threshold directly.

claimText: A 'LONG FINAL' report shall be made when an aircraft turns onto final at a distance greater than 7 km (4 NM) from touchdown.
normalizedRuleClaim: A LONG FINAL report is made when turning final more than 7 km/4 NM from touchdown.
notes: Likely needs trace-query support for distance-at-report before becoming a clean executable test.

claimText: The landing/touch and go/low approach clearance will include the runway designation.
normalizedRuleClaim: Landing, touch-and-go, and low-approach clearances include the runway designation.
notes: May already be structurally enforced by instruction constructors; useful as a boundary case where a new test may add little value.

claimText: ATC may clear an aircraft for a 'TOUCH AND GO' using the phrase 'CLEARED TOUCH AND GO'.
normalizedRuleClaim: ATC may clear an aircraft for TOUCH AND GO using the phrase CLEARED TOUCH AND GO.
notes: Executable, but less central than go-around recovery for the next task.

claimText: Any transmissions to aircraft going around shall be brief and kept to a minimum.
normalizedRuleClaim: Transmissions to aircraft going around should be brief and kept to a minimum.
notes: Important operational guidance but not a clean deterministic sim test without a phrase-length/content policy.

claimText: Unless absolutely necessary, controllers will not give taxi instructions to pilots until the landing roll is complete.
normalizedRuleClaim: Unless absolutely necessary, controllers do not give taxi instructions until the landing roll is complete.
notes: Goldens cover after-landing taxi flow, but a specific no-early-taxi invariant would need trace timing assertions.

claimText: Clearances and instructions to enter, land on, take off from, hold short of, cross, taxi and backtrack on any runway shall always be read back.
normalizedRuleClaim: Clearances and instructions to enter, land on, take off from, hold short of, cross, taxi, or backtrack on a runway are always read back.
notes: Excellent later family, but cross-cutting enough that it should not be the first vertical slice.

claimText: Readback must be in full and in the same sequence as given, with the condition first.
normalizedRuleClaim: A conditional-clearance readback is in full and in the same sequence as given, with the condition first.
notes: Useful contrast: source unit is precise, but the sim likely needs richer phrase/readback sequence representation before a meaningful test.
